one_sentence_story: In 1997 in Science, Wolfram Schultz, Peter Dayan, and Read Montague proved that midbrain dopamine neurons do NOT measure pleasure — they compute exact Reward Prediction Error (Actual Minus Expected): spiking for unexpected good news (+), going flat when expected rewards arrive on cue (0), and plunging below baseline when expected rewards fail to show (-).
so_what_for_you: Stop chasing endless novelty hits thinking the *next* purchase will finally lock in permanent dopamine: build **small unscheduled delights** (`Actual > Expected`) into work and love, mute **slot-machine notification badges**, and slow down to savor present enjoyment.

jargon_map.plain: the mathematical gap between how good an outcome actually was versus how good your brain predicted it would be
jargon_map.analogy: getting a $1,000 bonus when you expected $0 (+1000!), vs expecting $1,000 (0), vs expecting $2,000 (-1000 ouch!)

jargon_map.plain: once a light or chime reliably predicts a reward, the dopamine burst moves forward to the CUE and goes silent at the reward itself
jargon_map.analogy: getting excited at the ice-cream truck jingle down the block

jargon_map.plain: the sharp pause in VTA dopamine firing below baseline at the exact instant an expected reward fails to arrive
jargon_map.analogy: stepping onto a dark basement stair that isn't there

jargon_map.plain: updating future expectations step-by-step using live prediction errors — shared by midbrain VTA neurons and modern AI agents
distinguishing motivational pursuit/surprise learning from warm sensory pleasure
jargon_map.analogy: craving one more scroll at 1 AM without even enjoying it
